newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Slavneft sees 2.17 pct stake sale possible in July.
newsitem.headline: Slavneft sees 2.17 pct stake sale possible in July.

text.p: Russian-Belarussian oil company Slavneft said on Wednesday a government-owned 2.17 percent stake could be sold at a special auction in July, after agreement from the Belarussian government was received.
Slavneft chief executive Anatoly Fomin also said production would edge up to 12.95 million tonnes (259,000 barrels per day) in 1997 after 12.90 million tonnes (258,000 bpd) in 1996.
"We plan to produce 12.4 million tonnes (248,000 bpd) of oil in 1997...and counting joint ventures -- 12.95 million tonnes," Fomin told a news conference after the annual shareholders meeting.
Slavneft refineries would increase output by 800,000 tonnes compared to 1996, he added. Slavneft processed 12.0 million tonnes of oil in 1996.

Fomin said the oil company was almost ready to carry out the auction of the 2.17 percent stake but did not say if there would be special conditions regarding foreign participation: "I hope that we will soon get written agreement from the Belarussian government for carrying out the auction and sometime in July we will carry it out."

He said two investment tenders previously planned for May or the end of June for a 15 percent stake and a 4.8 percent stake -- for non-residents and residents respectively -- had been put off due to the 2.17 percent special auction.
